records.text: On 2023-05-20, the user was looking for new vegan recipe ideas, especially vegan lasagna, and was interested in trying mushroom-based bolognese and oat milk in béchamel sauce.

The user said a Netflix documentary about the environmental impact of the meat industry opened their eyes to the benefits of a vegetarian lifestyle. The user had since been experimenting with plant-based recipes and cooking techniques and found plant-based alternatives inspiring and versatile.

On 2023-05-20, the assistant suggested vegan lasagna variations: roasted vegetables with cashew- or tofu-based ricotta; mushroom-and-lentil bolognese with vegan ricotta and spinach; spinach and artichoke with dairy-free béchamel; vegan meatball lasagna; and butternut squash and sage with cashew béchamel. Suggested resources included Oh My Veggies, The Full Helping, Vegan Richa, Food52, and Lucky Vitamin.

For mushroom bolognese, the assistant recommended combining mushroom varieties such as cremini, shiitake, and porcini; chopping them finely; avoiding overcooking; thickening with a flour-and-fat roux; balancing richness with red wine, balsamic vinegar, or tomato paste; and simmering for at least 30 minutes. For oat milk béchamel, the assistant recommended unsweetened, unflavored oat milk, constant whisking over low heat, and adjusting thickener as needed.

On 2023-05-20, the assistant suggested vegan cheese sauces: cashew; nutritional-yeast and cooked-vegetable; soy-yogurt; cashew-based vegan mozzarella; and roasted-vegetable sauces. Suggested seasonings included nutritional yeast, garlic powder, onion powder, and smoked paprika; suggested thickeners included cornstarch, flour, agar agar, and tapioca starch.

The user had been using oat milk and said it was working well, but wanted to try other plant-based milk options. The user asked for recommendations for a good non-dairy yogurt; no recommendation was given in this conversation segment.

Vegan quiche suggestions given to the user included flaky or gluten-free crusts, blind-baking a crust for 10–12 minutes, and baking at 375°F (190°C) for 35–40 minutes. Suggested fillings included roasted vegetables, mushrooms with lentils, and spinach with artichokes.
Vegan butter alternatives suggested to the user included Miyoko's Kitchen, Daiya Vegan Butter, Nuttelex, coconut oil, avocado oil, and homemade vegan butter.

On 2023-05-20, the user planned to create an implementation plan for a business called the Fresh Earth Ecosystem, beginning with the first components the business will launch. The user intended to provide information about the technology vision first, then details about the individual components, so the assistant would have context before working on the implementation plan.

The Fresh Earth Ecosystem’s Project Management Platform is intended to connect global stakeholders working on regenerative health and regenerative land projects. It supports designing, implementing, and commercializing validated programs, with project creation and management, data analysis and visualization, B2B marketplace support, validation systems, and group management tools. Intended participants include health and farm experts, suppliers, universities, government, policymakers, and end-users. Goals include innovation, lower costs, efficiency, shared knowledge, transparency, and positive change in the agri-food system.

On May 23, 2023, the user planned to make fertilizer from kitchen scraps and eggshells, an idea learned at a gardening workshop the previous weekend.

It recommended roughly two-thirds brown to one-third green materials, layering brown and green materials, keeping the pile as moist as a damp sponge, turning it every 7–10 days, crushing eggshells, and using a roughly 3×3×3-foot bin or pile. The assistant estimated composting could take 2–3 months and suggested sifting finished compost.

The user asked whether banana peels could be added to the compost mix, noting that they had heard banana peels are high in potassium and beneficial for the garden. The assistant said yes, and advised chopping them, adding them in moderation (suggesting one part banana peels to ten parts other compost materials), and balancing them with other compost materials.

The user had been saving coffee grounds and asked whether they could be added to the compost mix. The assistant said yes and advised adding them in moderation (suggesting one part coffee grounds to ten parts other compost materials), mixing them with carbon-rich brown materials, and avoiding excessive amounts.

The user is developing the fictional tidally heated forest moon Xylophia-IV-e as an ecopunk setting. Across most of the moon, altitude is a major determinant of climate, except at the extreme latitudes and in a narrow equatorial strip. The moon is generally very humid, has regular rainfall, and rarely becomes very hot or cold; freezing likely occurs only at the highest altitudes and possibly sometimes in circumpolar regions.

The user envisions Xylophia-IV-e having humid subtropical climates at middle altitudes over most of the moon; highland rainforest at the highest altitudes in middle latitudes, extending up to the snow lines; Mediterranean climate around salt lakes; tropical rainforest in the equatorial band; and hemiboreal or boreal rainforest in circumpolar regions.

On most of Xylophia-IV-e, conifers grow from the snow lines down to ravine floors. They are absent from salt flats around salt lakes, scrub surrounding those flats, and wetlands around brackish deltas that transition into the scrub and flats.

On Xylophia-IV-e, hardwood trees bearing nuts, seeds, and fruit are abundant from middle altitudes downward. Palm-like trees appear in the lower part of the middle altitudes and become very numerous at the lowest altitudes closest to the salt lakes.

In the user's speculative setting, ravines are cut by seismic cracks and further gouged by erosion from brackish rivers. The sheer gorge faces expose countless lava tubes where the ravines have divided the rock.
The user estimates that, except at the lowest and highest latitudes and altitudes, temperatures on the setting's world rarely, if ever, fall outside 13°C to 25°C.

On 2023-05-24, the user asked that each abstract they provide be summarized in exactly two sentences, in third person, using APA-style in-text citations for the authors. They want all summaries from a set combined into one paragraph, without labels such as “first set” or “second set.” Abstracts are formatted with authors, year, and abstract text.

Xu, Yiwen, Cheng, Li, and Zhang (2020) studied noise pollution and economic development using monitoring data from 111 Chinese cities (1991–2017). They found an inverted N-shaped relationship nationally, with an inverted N shape in eastern China, an inverted U shape in central China, and a linear relationship in western China; tertiary-industry development was associated with increased noise pollution.
records.topic: Environmental Kuznets Curve and noise pollution in China

records.text: Lu, Venevsky, Shi, Wang, Wright, and Wu (2021) examined carbon intensity of human well-being and economic development in eight Chinese economic zones from 1997 to 2015. Seven zones showed advances toward sustainability, represented by downward turning points in inverted-N Environmental Kuznets Curves, between 2012 and 2015; the Northwestern zone had not reached this point by 2015.
records.topic: Environmental Kuznets Curve and sustainability in China

records.text: Chen, Zhang, Wu, and Cai (2020) used corrected NPP-VIIRS nighttime-light data to estimate CO2 emissions at provincial and city scales in China and examined 291 cities. They found that the city-scale Environmental Kuznets Curve exists, emissions were higher in western, economically developed, and industry- and mining-dominated cities, and the provincial emissions estimates had an R² of 0.85 compared with statistical values.
records.topic: City-level CO2 emissions and Environmental Kuznets Curve in China

records.text: He and Lin (2019) used provincial panel data from 2003–2017 and a panel smooth transition autoregression model to study regional differences in China’s Environmental Kuznets Curve. They found pollution emissions and energy intensity decrease stepwise from western to eastern China, an inverted U-shaped relationship for energy intensity with a threshold of 0.7670, and an energy-intensity transition threshold of 0.9168 between high and low regimes; more-developed eastern provinces generally exceeded the threshold during the study period.
records.topic: Regional Environmental Kuznets Curve and energy intensity in China

records.text: On 2023-05-24, the user asked for a bullet-point summary of a methods section from “Efficient Self-supervised Learning with Contextualized Target Representations for Vision, Speech and Language.” The section describes a Data2vec-based method that predicts contextualized teacher representations for masked parts of samples.
entities: Efficient Self-supervised Learning with Contextualized Target Representations for Vision, Speech and Language

records.text: The paper’s method encodes only unmasked portions of a sample with the student encoder, then uses a lightweight convolutional decoder to predict the teacher network’s contextualized representations for masked portions. The teacher targets incorporate information from the full unmasked sample and are formed by averaging normalized activations from the teacher’s top K feed-forward network blocks.
entities: Efficient Self-supervised Learning with Contextualized Target Representations for Vision, Speech and Language

records.text: The teacher weights are an exponential moving average of the student encoder weights, with the averaging coefficient increasing linearly from an initial value to a final value over a scheduled number of updates. The student is trained to match teacher targets using an L2 loss.
entities: Efficient Self-supervised Learning with Contextualized Target Representations for Vision, Speech and Language

records.text: The model uses modality-specific feature encoders and a Transformer. The paper describes 16×16-pixel patch mapping for vision, a multilayer convolutional feature encoder for speech, and byte-pair-encoding-based learned embeddings for text. Masked positions are represented with random Gaussian noise; the convolutional decoder uses layer normalization, GELU activations, and residual connections.
entities: Efficient Self-supervised Learning with Contextualized Target Representations for Vision, Speech and Language

records.text: Multi-mask training reuses the same teacher representation as the target for M different masked versions of a training sample, amortizing the cost of teacher computation. The method also shares feature-encoder outputs across masked versions to avoid redundant computation, especially benefiting dense modalities such as speech.
entities: Efficient Self-supervised Learning with Contextualized Target Representations for Vision, Speech and Language

records.text: Inverse block masking selects contiguous blocks to preserve rather than selecting blocks to mask. It aims to give the student contiguous context for learning semantic representations. Blocks can overlap, causing variation in the number of masked positions; the method adjusts individual positions so each sample in a batch has the desired number of unmasked positions.
entities: Efficient Self-supervised Learning with Contextualized Target Representations for Vision, Speech and Language
